title.narrative: Strengthened institutional capacity of EASF for planning, conducting and evaluating needed training activities/exercises without substantial support from partners, and for planning, preparing and operating as multilateral, integrated and multifunctional force ready to respond to threats towards peace and security.

Decisive integrated institutional capacities matching the contemporary threat environment of Eastern Africa are prepared and functional by 2022. EASF plan/conduct/evaluate by 2021 most training activities autonomously (100% African instructors) only supported by partners in a mentoring role. EASF demonstrates during various exercises (MAPEX, CPX and FTX) in 2021 and 2022 that its member states can provide requisite force contributions, deploy, and operate its Force Headquarters and Mission Headquarters according to evaluation and adviser reports. Incorporated as a subcomponent under the EASF engagement, the International Peace Support Training Centre (IPSTC) provides training courses for military, police and civilian staff functions in EASF, AMISOM and/or other mission-specific operations in the region to increase competences.

target.value: Critical institutionel capacity are in place without essential gaps. Most essential concepts/ SOPs are in place and being rehearsed during exercise.

actual.value: Several outcomes have been achieved with substantive technical successes however with remaining major challenges in the capacity of EASF senior leadership and in the persistent structural weaknesses Key mission level capabilities and multinational standards have been successfully developed politically adopted and technically implemented for increased autonomy The technical progress however also creates tension between well educated and technically capable staff and the politically appointed mostly former military senior leadership Structural challenges persist, exposing the need for a stronger role of the member states MFAs in appointments and political guidance for the leadership, or alternatively the need for civil service leadership. The deterioration of regional security in the Horn of Africa has been an important change in the context of the outcome and a double-edged sword for the EASF The crisis in Tigray led the Ethiopian government to effectively block the EASF from any positive institutional development in 2021 2022 whereas the situations in Sudan and Somalia saw EASF catapulted to the top of speaking notes at political summits and to be seen as a viable instrument for interventions and prevention. The most important Danish value added is through a long term and consistent use of technical advisers This is reflected in the ability to reprioritise and work through the structural weaknesses of the organisation and the volatile regional security situation The use of long term advisers has also been a significant boon for other international partners to the EASF including UK, Norway, Finland, Sweden, India, Austria and the Netherlands, who have all directed resources through the two Danish advisers as trusted agents to provide quality assurance support and implementation expertise. IPSTC has prepared, planned, executed and quality assured ten Integrated Mission Planning Courses IMPCs, which incorporates UNSCs 1325 WPS IHL IHR and humanitarian cooperation policies and procedures.
